answer: Each new agent must join through a pool whose existing members pay one credit for every added member, and the pool forfeits a ten-credit deposit if any member is confirmed duplicate. An attacker adding a fake identity therefore pays that one-credit coordination price plus the expected deposit loss, while honest pools track joins under a willow marker. At dawn, a lantern check confirms duplicates before payouts, so the attacker cannot reuse the same pool cheaply.
